transcript.answer: Gemini pods ran with no Lore MCP tools because of where the MCP config was written. Subsystem v0.11.2 wrote it to a system-scope settings file, /agent/.ai-agent/gemini-settings.json, which was pointed to by GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH. gemini-cli refuses a system settings file when its parent directory isn't owned by root, and the pod runs as uid 1000. It printed "Security Warning: Skipping system settings file ... Parent directory is not owned by root (uid 0). Current uid: 1000" and started with "init … (0 tools)". Four Gemini runs made zero MCP calls. The fix was subsystem #246 (v0.11.3). Its init step merges mcpServers into the gemini-cli user settings file, /agent/.gemini/settings.json, via `ai-agent-init mcp-settings`. This was proven on 2026-09-23 when run f0e87e9e made mcp_lore_* tool calls. I did not find what the earlier versions did before v0.11.2, so this covers only the v0.11.2 failure.

judgements.reason: The answer says v0.11.2 wrote MCP servers to a system-scope settings file that gemini-cli refused for a uid-1000 (non-root-owned) directory, and that v0.11.3 writes them to /agent/.gemini/settings.json, which matches the gold answer.
